passed_evidence: The exact 52,608-row pre-2025 H1 corpus, frozen prior, manifest and runner hashes passed, and two independent runs were byte-identical.
The primary had enough Design and Validation interventions and preserved Validation unrealized PnL, terminal inventory count, underwater duration and annual drawdown breadth.
All primary and neighbor realized, unrealized, total PnL, drawdown, holding, utilization, underwater and terminal-inventory ledgers remained visible under equal capital.
material_learning: The published positive return-predictability result for a full-distribution realized-performance statistic did not transfer into DRA entry-selection economics at H1 resolution. The primary veto removed profitable participation in both windows, reduced realized PnL, worsened Validation holding times and won only one annual total-PnL comparison. The permissive neighbor did nothing in Validation, while the stricter neighbor nearly doubled Validation drawdown and more than doubled P90 holding. This is neither an independent alpha nor a useful risk veto.
scientific_claim: For the exact H1 Schnytzer-Westreich root, prior-20-day midrank percentile, 0.5 primary and 0.4/0.6 neighbors applied only to unchanged equal-capital DRA V1 entries, historical Design and Validation evidence through 2024 rejects candidate status. The result does not authorize another percentile, root approximation, lookback, sampling interval, return definition or realized-moment rescue.
uncertainty: This is historical preregistered Design and Validation evidence through 2024, not independent post-selection OOS or forward profitability.
The H1 root is much coarser than the five-minute estimator in the primary paper, but that limitation does not authorize a paid or unsealed higher-frequency backfill.
The conclusion closes only the exact percentile admission transfer; it does not dispute the paper's regression evidence in its own sample.
